name: Omri
overview: Omri was a male commander of the army who became king over Israel, noted in Scripture for his significant leadership role. His reign is marked by a pronounced wickedness, as he "did evil in the sight of the LORD, and acted more wickedly than all who were before him." This characterization highlights his failure to uphold God's standards during his rule.
namesAndTitles: The name Omri means 'thrive' or 'live long,' reflecting a proper name of Hebrew origin. Additionally, he held the title 'King of Israel,' denoting his political authority over the nation. Neither the name nor the title is recorded as being given by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture infers that Omri was the father of Ahab, establishing a dynastic link within the monarchy of Israel. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Omri's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his role as a military leader who ascended to kingship and whose reign is characterized by unprecedented evil compared to his predecessors. His leadership set a negative spiritual precedent for Israel, influencing the nation's moral and religious decline. This legacy is critical for understanding the challenges faced by Israel during and after his rule.
